title: Third-party scorer payloads (TruLens, Ragas, DeepEval, Phoenix judges): reject api_base and gateway destination keys in kwargs at any depth
answers: Why does registering a TruLens or Ragas judge with a custom api_base now return 400?
Where are third-party scorer kwargs checked for destination hosts or SSRF?
How do I point a third-party judge at a custom LLM endpoint now that api_base is rejected?
Is an ensemble or MemAlign scorer that wraps a TruLens judge with api_base still accepted?
body:
Path: Serialized scorer payloads sent to the register-scorer, scorer/invoke and genai evaluate invoke endpoints (inline, or re-fetched from the tracking store) pass through mlflow/server/handlers.py:_validate_serialized_scorer_payload, which calls mlflow/utils/validation.py:_validate_third_party_scorer_data for every `third_party_scorer_data.kwargs` block (TruLens, Ragas, DeepEval, Phoenix judges), including ones nested in ensemble or MemAlign `base_judge` scorers.
Rule: Walk the whole serialized payload with `_iter_third_party_scorer_data`, then for each block require `kwargs` to be a JSON object or null, and reject any key in GATEWAY_DESTINATION_KEYS (`api_base`, `base_url`, `model_list`, `fallbacks`, `custom_llm_provider`) found by `_find_destination_keys` at any depth. That search also counts `[key, value]` two-item lists, because `dict()` turns them into a mapping during deserialization. Root cause: kwargs reach the wrapped library's LLM client unchanged (the TruLens LiteLLM fallback forwards them into litellm.completion), so the caller chose the host the server connects to. The fix is a server-side check before any deserialization or job submission.
Symptom: A caller could register or invoke a judge with kwargs.api_base pointing at an internal address, and the server would connect there when the scorer ran (SSRF). A top-level-only check let the same key through when it was nested in an ensemble, in completion_kwargs, or in a list of pairs.
Constraints: Not gated by MLFLOW_SERVER_ENABLE_CUSTOM_SCORERS; relaxing the decorator exec guard must not relax this. Payloads without these keys are untouched. Custom endpoints belong on the server, via a `gateway:/` endpoint or provider environment variables. Applies to server-side handling only.
applies: Server-side validation of third-party scorer kwargs in mlflow/utils/validation.py and its callers in mlflow/server/handlers.py; not client-side scorer construction.
says: Registering a third-party evaluation judge with a custom endpoint URL returns an error.
Running evaluation jobs fails when nested judge configurations specify custom destination hosts.
Connect registered evaluation judges to custom model endpoints through approved gateway configurations.
Block server-side request forgery vulnerabilities caused by custom host destinations in evaluation judges.
search: Server-side validation in mlflow/server/handlers.py:_validate_serialized_scorer_payload and mlflow/utils/validation.py:_validate_third_party_scorer_data rejects any GATEWAY_DESTINATION_KEYS (including api_base, base_url, model_list, fallbacks, and custom_llm_provider) found at any depth inside third-party scorer kwargs. Payloads are checked across standalone, ensemble, and MemAlign base_judge configurations using _iter_third_party_scorer_data and _find_destination_keys to prevent SSRF from reaching backend completion clients. Applies solely to server-side endpoints and is not relaxed by MLFLOW_SERVER_ENABLE_CUSTOM_SCORERS, with custom endpoints belonging on the server via gateway endpoints or environment variables.
